question: Should both OpenGrep workflows adopt a 10-second connection timeout and 120-second total installer-download deadline?
rationale: The code correctly enforces the proposed bounds, but choosing when a security scan should fail on a slow upstream response is an operational CI policy decision owned by the OpenGrep workflow maintainers.

options.title: Approve the proposed bounds
options.body: Keep the 10/120-second limits after correcting the guard assertions, accepting bounded scan failures during exceptionally slow upstream responses.

options.title: Retune the transfer deadline
options.body: Choose a longer maximum transfer time if maintainers prefer greater tolerance for transient GitHub raw-content slowness.

options.title: Retain only the outer timeout
options.body: Decline per-download limits and continue relying on the workflow-level timeout, preserving tolerance at the cost of potentially long stuck scans.

recommendation.title: Approve the proposed bounds
recommendation.body: Keep the 10/120-second limits after correcting the guard assertions, accepting bounded scan failures during exceptionally slow upstream responses.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and documented the affected OpenGrep workflows and are the strongest history-backed owner for their operational timeout policy.
